recipes.name: Biscotti
ingredients_raw: 1 tablespoon anise extract, or 3 drops anise oil

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Grease two cookie sheets or line with parchment paper.
Beat sugar, oil, eggs, and anise extract together in a medium bowl until well-blended. Combine flour and baking powder in a separate bowl; stir into egg mixture to form a heavy dough.
Divide dough into two equal pieces. Form each piece into a log the length of a cookie sheet. Place one log on each of the prepared sheets; and press dough down to 1/2-inch thickness.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown, 25 to 30 minutes. Transfer logs to wire racks; let sit until cool enough to handle, about 15 minutes.
Slice each log crosswise into about eighteen 1/2-inch-thick slices. Place slices cut-sides up back on the cookie sheets.
Bake until lightly toasted and golden brown, 6 to 10 minutes per side.

raw_recipe.headline: Biscotti
raw_recipe.description: Biscotti are twice-baked Italian cookies that are wonderfully light, crisp, and perfect for dipping in coffee. Drizzle with chocolate for a delicious festive gift.

review.reviewBody: This is absolutely the best...crispy, crunchy, mild sweet flavor...not like the tooth-breaking commercial biscotti. I baked this for the first time last week exactly as printed with exception of using almond flavoring instead of anise. Like some others I found the baking time needed was less than the recipe stated, so watch it closely. Here are few tips that I'd suggest to those with less than satisfactory results. Do NOT add more flour. Stir it up as the recipe states and then divide the dough directly onto your well greased baking sheets. Use your hands to form it into a long roll that goes the length of the sheets and then use your fingers or a rolling pin (I used my Pampered Chef little roller) to flatten it out to a rectangle about 4" wide and about 1/2" thick. Bake. Remove from oven and while still hot use a pizza cutter to cut into strips. Flip strips on their sides and return to oven, continuing as the recipe directs. This worked absolutely perfectly for me and was so much easier than transferring a pre-formed roll of sticky dough to the baking pan and then contending with trying to slice a cool (and very crumbly) finished product. Hope this will help some of you and encourage you to try again. It's soooo easy and so tasty with ingredients just as they are! Wish I could give it more stars! I can't keep my hands out of the cookie jar!

Delicious! Great with coffee or as a snack. I did not have anise so used 1/2 Tbsp. almond and 1/2 Tbsp. vanilla intstead. Great flavor! TIP: Once dough is made; get a couple of long sheets of wax paper and split dough into 2 equal parts; place dough half on wax sheet and fold excess wax over dough allowing room for expanision; apply pressure/shape dough without having it stick to your hands or your kitchen counter. Do same with second half. Good luck!

I cannot say enough good things about this recipe! THANK YOU SO MUCH! I have personalized it for my family and have made it many times now. Instead of 1 cup sugar, we add half cup each of white and brown. Throw in 1 cup chopped almonds, (some finely chopped and others coarse)- mix in with flour,add 1 tbsp. almond extract and 1/2 tbsp vanilla to the wet ingredients. This time I am also adding some chopped dry cherries, then you can drizzle with melted chocolate or almond bark for a special flair. Sad thing is, now my husband doesn't want to go to the coffee shop anymore - he insists these biscotti are so great - why buy them! (I do agree, so now does anyone have a good cappuccino recipe they'll share? :) THank you Jandee! PS - these make incredibly elegant (not to mention EASY) gifts for anyone you care about!

375°F oven temperature is too hot, Biscotti started to burn after a few minutes. Dough is too sticky and difficult to form into logs, best omit the oil. Tweaked the recipe: 3 C flour, 1C sugar, no oil, 1t Baking Powder, 1/4t salt, 3 lg. eggs at room temperature. Baked at 350°F for 25 minutes, cooled, sliced 3/4" thick, and then toasted in 300°F oven, 10 minutes per side, added 1/2C sliced toasted almonds, Vanilla extract, Almond Extract, and lemon zest...Much Better

Absolutely delicious. I read a lot of reviews before making the biscotti. I made two different batches. One with the anise extract with nuts and white chocolate morsels and second batch with vanilla extract, almond extract, chopped almonds and white chocolate morsels. Both delicious but my favorite was the biscotti using the anise extract. Next time I will increase the extract amount for even more flavor. I agree with some of the reviewers to bring the cooking time down to 18 minutes and then 6 minutes on each side. But this also depends on your oven and if you prefer the biscottI hard or a bit soft. I found the flavor of the cookies seem to intensity more so after a day. These are really really good. Thank you so much for sharing this great recipe.

I used this to make biscotti spoons. I have a silicon mold that I am making candy spoons in and got a hairbrain idea about biscotti spoons. I tried this recipe and it worked perfect! I rolled the dough in ropes, laying and twisting it into the silicon mold then patting down with my fingers. 15 minutes to bake. I thought with just the first bake, they were perfect. Next step is dipping and decorating with chocolate!
I used almond extract instead of anise and drizzled some chocolate. Fave reviews! Took the suggestion of another reviewer and used the pizza cutter right out of the oven and it works great!

I used more anise and put in the grated peel of one lemon and one orange. I also turned the temp down to 350 for the first bake and then to 325 for the second bake. When they were done and cooled I dipped them on one side with a mixture of melted chocolate and 1 tsp of crisco shortening. They take a little long to dry but they are worth the wait.

I have been making biscottis for decades and this is a classic recipe! It was a brilliant suggestion to use a pizza cutter and cut the cookies after they come out of oven to toast them..that is a game changer!!

Ok so you can do a blend of the three spices. I used a tablespoon of vanilla and a teaspoon of star anise (ran out) and a teaspoonful of almond extract. Turned out well. Also would not that you can use crisco or coconut oil as a substitute to vegetable oil. Just warm it 30 seconds at a time and whisk. Make sure you don’t get too hot, as this will cause your eggs to be scrambled eggs. You want some solid that you whisk away. May take a min or so. The crust turned out right between biscotti and shortbread. I personally think biscotti is a bit too hard. You can whisk hersheys chocolate across in a flinging motion, for a neat looking slight chocolate flavor. I also added almonds on top pressed in. Next time I will incorporate. Overall a good recipe

I used this as written except I added slivered almonds, dried cranberries and almond flavoring and added white chocolate drizzles over the top (candy making drops, melted). It was pretty good! It was very easy and my first time making biscotti. I cut with a pizza cutter when it was still hot, turned the pieces on their sides and returned to the oven for a few minutes. Everyone thought it was really good but I personally would have liked it a bit sweeter. Next time I will try orange extract with cranberry and almonds and a little more sugar. Overall this is a great recipie and so easy.

Loved the recipe. Easy to follow and very little ingredients. I used unrefined coconut oil instead and a little vanilla instead of anise. The coconut oil gave it a slight toasted coconut taste and smell.

This biscotti recipe is fantastic!!! I used vanilla extract instead of anise, for preference and used half olive oil and half vegetable oil rather than all vegetable and you couldn’t taste it at all. I added some cinnamon as well and it is really delicious!! The absolute perfect texture too— not too hard. Well loved by all!
I used vanilla instead of anise and added hazelnuts and mini chocolate chips. Absolutely delicious

I have made biscotti so many times over my life using many recipes. They all are pretty much the same in basic ingredients. The customization is the signature of each cook. I like almond and orange with white chocolate. This is the best basic recipe I have ever seen. It is consistent and reliable. It also teaches a cooking technique of twice baking. This recipe is just about perfect.
I substituted vanilla extract for the anise and added 1/2 cup of candied fruit peel. They are delicious!
I followed this recipe exact.. then on parchment paper, middle of oven at 375 and after 20 minutes the bottoms were completely black burnt !

I ground up some leftover star anise I had in the cupboard. I didn't have the anise oil. I used 1 tsp in this recipe. I could have added a bit more but honestly, they turned out great and everyone loved them. I dipped them in chocolate then sprinkled finely chopped walnuts. The chocolate was made of semi sweet chips and oil. It stays soft. Next time I would use a chocolate that hardens a bit.

This is a perfect recipe that can be easily tweaked to your liking. I like to add things like a cup of toasted chopped almonds, dried fruits, change up the flavors with either different extracts, or ground spices into the flour. The possibilities are endless!
Wonderful recipe! I’ve tried several in the past and products were somewhat crumbly; these are easier to work with. Did not use anise,subbed vanilla extract.
